question.leadin: This outspoken critic of the death penalty executed thousands of political opponents during his reign of power on the Committee of Public Safety.
question.text: Name this "public accuser" who promoted the Cult of the Supreme Being and guillotined [GEE-uh-teen'd] supporters of the monarchy during the "Reign of Terror."
question.answerHtml: Maximilien Robespierre [“robes”-p’yair] (or Maximilien François Marie Isidore de Robespierre )
question.clue: Originally a lawyer from Arras, this man opposed Jean-Jacques Brissot's warmongering and sponsored the Cult of the Supreme Being.

swap.leadin: Gebhard von Blucher (BLOO-ker) and his Prussian troops aided the British at this battle.
swap.text: Name this battle, a decisive 1815 defeat for Napoleon Bonaparte in Belgium that ended the Hundred Days and was his final defeat.
swap.clue: The absence of General Grouchy deprived the losers of one third of their army.

question.leadin: This commander claimed to be able to hear St. Margaret and St. Catherine speaking to her.
question.text: Name this peasant girl, who commanded French troops to victory in the Siege of Orleans ["orr-lee-ON"]. She was later burned at the stake by the English.
question.clue: Pierre Cauchon, the Bishop of Beauvais, led the interrogation of this person, who was captured by Burgundian forces.

swap.text: This author of J'Accuse also wrote about the rise of a courtesan in Nana and about a failed coal miner's strike in Germinal.
swap.clue: Outraged by the events, this French author published "J'accuse."

question.leadin: Answer the following about Robert Curthose.
question.text: Robert Curthose was the son of William the Conqueror, a ruler of this duchy who later conquered England in 1066.
question.clue: The second ranger battalion climbed up the Pointe du Hoc during this action.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the War of the First Coalition.
swap.text: During the conflict, this island birthplace of Napoleon revolted against the French to form a British-sponsored kingdom before returning to French rule in 1796.
swap.clue: An independence leader on this island founded a university at the fortified mountain town of Corte and promulgated a constitution which established a separation of powers and a ban on vendettas.

question.leadin: A ruler from this dynasty fought three civil wars against his sons after they accused his wife Judith of Bavaria of infidelity.
question.text: Name this medieval dynasty. The queen Bertrada from this dynasty pushed her son Carloman out of power to help her other son Charlemagne.
question.clue: A member of this dynasty granted the territory of the future Papal States to Stephen II in a so-called "donation."

swap.leadin: This monarch's brother Charles led the League of the Public Weal against him, and signed the Treaty of Picquigny with England.
swap.text: Name this French king whose scheming earned him the nickname "The Universal Spider."
swap.clue: While he was the dauphin, this ruler joined the "Praguerie" against his father.

question.text: This dynasty lends its name to a variant of Latin script used in many 8th century manuscripts. This dynasty was founded by Clovis I in 509.
question.clue: In a confiict caused by a princess's refusal to follow her husband's religious practices, this dynasty defeated Amalric, king of the Visigoths.

swap.leadin: Name these successors of Francis I.
swap.text: This king's persecutions of Huguenots were influenced by his mother, Catherine de Medici. During his reign, he authorized the St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre of 1572 to cover up the death of Admiral Coligny.
swap.clue: A son of Catherine de Medici, his mother and later Coligny effectively ruled, as this man was crowned at age ten. His 1574 death ended a war-torn reign.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the American African offensive in World War II.
question.text: Eisenhower made a deal with this notorious Nazi collaborator which allowed him to bypass fighting the Vichy forces and move his troops east towards Rommel's Afrika Korps.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about crusades that occured in Europe.
swap.text: In addition to the Fourth Crusade, Innocent III sanctioned this crusade in Southern France against a heretical gnostic sect whose dualist beliefs are often compared with the Bulgarian Bogomil ["BO-guh-mil"] sect.
swap.clue: It was spurred by Peter of Castelnau's assassination at the orders of Raymond VI, and finally ended by Louis VIII.

question.leadin: King Francis I, who had turned 21 the day before, asked to be knighted after his victory in this battle.
question.text: Name this battle in which the French army defeated a large force of Swiss mercenaries, resulting in Switzerland later declaring perpetual neutrality. This battle is often described as showing the superiority of artillery over traditional phalanx tactics.
question.clue: Prior to this battle, a treaty was signed which awarded Massimilano Sforza the booby prize of the Duchy of Nemours.

swap.text: This French commander-in-chief ordered the attack on Alexander von Kluck's First Army which began the First Marne.
swap.clue: This French commander became known as "the Victor of the Marne." He resigned from command after being blamed for the French army's lack of preparation for Germany's 1916 attack on Verdun.

question.leadin: Horse manure and the microclimate created by this place caused the "pink of the fields" mushroom to be cultivated in the 1800s.
question.text: Name this place to which bones from the Holy Innocents cemetery were transferred, stabilizing a sinking city.
question.answerHtml: Paris catacombs [or Catacombs of Paris; or Catacombes de Paris]

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Crimean War, in which several Eurasian powers ganged up to fight Russia.
swap.text: This European leader helped provoke the war by demanding sovereignty over Christian sites in the Holy Land, which the Ottomans refused and gave to Russia instead.
swap.answerHtml: Louis-Napoleon Bonaparte [or Napoleon III; do not prompt on “Napoleon”]
swap.clue: This ruler abdicated after losing to Helmuth von Moltke's troops in the Franco-Prussian War.

question.leadin: Name the following more or less real people or events that figure in opera plots.
question.text: The action of Tosca is briefly interrupted by the announcement of Napoleon's victory at this 1800 battle, at which he defeated Melas and the Austrians, gained control of Italy south of the Po, and precipitated the end of the Second Coalition
question.clue: One side fended off cavalry charges until the arrival of the Consular Guard, yet an attack on Castel Ceriolo failed just as Victor's men could hold on no longer, after which General Zach took over for his wounded leader.

swap.text: The Jansenist theologian Francois de Paris was buried in a cemetery at this church in Paris, which became a pilgrimage site for religious pilgrims called convulsionnaires who beat and stabbed each other while thrashing around in fits.

question.leadin: This man collaborated with Georges Duby on the five volume History of Private Life.
question.text: Name this historiographer, likely best known for his study of the child and the family in the ancien regime, which was translated into English as Centuries of Childhood.

swap.leadin: J'Accuse anyone who zero's this bonus of being horrible at quiz bowl, like Leo Wolpert. FTPE.
swap.text: "J'Accuse" was addressed to this president of the Third Republic, who was succeeded by Emile Loubet. Urban legend holds he died from a stroke while either screwing or getting head from his mistress.
swap.clue: This member of the Opportunist Republicans won his only election as a compromise candidate after the winner of a first-round plurality, Henri Brisson, was taken off of the ballot.
